title: I built a free browser detective mystery with AI assistance — Room 307
author: carcheckdk
selftext:
I recently released my first short browser detective game, **Room 307: The Last Message**.

The player investigates a hotel disappearance by examining documents, comparing witness statements, and supporting deductions with evidence.

I used generative AI extensively during development, particularly for story writing, programming, and iteration. One of the biggest challenges was making the mystery feel like a real investigation rather than just a collection of documents with obvious answers.

I worked through several versions, refining the evidence, deduction mechanics, and story structure.

The result is a free 10–20 minute browser mystery. I'm now testing it with real players before deciding whether to build a longer game.

**Play here:** [https://wellbel.itch.io/room-307-the-last-message](https://wellbel.itch.io/room-307-the-last-message)

I'd be interested to hear from other AI-assisted game developers: how do you evaluate whether your first playable prototype is actually engaging, rather than just technically functional?
